newsitem.title: PERU: Tremor hits Peruvian coast, no damage reported.
newsitem.headline: Tremor hits Peruvian coast, no damage reported.

text.p: A tremor measuring 4.4 on the Richter scale shook parts of Peru's central coast and Andean mountains on Wednesday causing panic in populated areas, but there were no immediate reports of damage, officials said.
The epicentre of the tremor that occurred at 9.52 a.m. (1452 GMT) was 260 miles (415 km) to the north of Lima, just south of the coastal city of Chimbote, according to Peru's Geophysics Institute.
Schoolchildren in Chimbote fled screaming from shaking buildings, according to local radio station Radioprogramas. Chimbote police said the tremor was strong but caused no damage.
The tremor, whose epicentre's depth was 22 miles (35 km) under the sea, also shook the Andean mountains to the east of Chimbote in the Santa valley.
Tremors and earthquakes frequently rock parts of Peru. The country's worst disaster caused by seismic movement happened in Ancash in 1970, when a landslide buried 70,000 people.
